task_title: QA filing: CF-241 (CF-206 shipped patch is unapplyable) + reopen CF-206 AC6
task_criteria: Filing-only criterion. Do NOT evaluate or require the underlying fix: row CF-241 is pending by design and the repair is future work it tracks, so nothing about fleet_ops_check.py or patches/ is expected to change in this commit. Verify only the filing. (1) `git show --name-only HEAD` names exactly `.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl` and `.coding-hermes/board/events.jsonl`. (2) On the committed board, `git show HEAD:.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl | jq -r 'select(.id=="CF-241") | [.status, ((.probe//"")|length)] | @tsv'` prints `pending` with a probe length greater than 0, and `git show HEAD:.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl | jq -r 'select(.id=="CF-206") | .status'` prints `in_progress`. (3) The probe extracted from the COMMITTED board runs from the repository root and prints one line carrying `patch=patches/fleet-ops-shell-toolkit.patch` and `apply_check_rc=`: `git show HEAD:.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl | jq -r 'select(.id=="CF-241").probe' > /tmp/cf241-probe.sh && bash /tmp/cf241-probe.sh`. Quote its literal output; a repaired tree printing `apply_check_rc=0` also passes this leg, because the criterion grades that the probe runs and reports a measured value, not which value. (4) `bash tests/selftest.sh` prints `SELFTEST: PASS` and `bash scripts/boardctl validate` prints `RESULT: OK`.
